newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Roche says Q1 sales of top drugs well up.
newsitem.headline: Roche says Q1 sales of top drugs well up.

text.p: Roche Holding AG said U.S. sales of its Rivotril/Klonopin and Toradol drugs had fallen sharper than expected in the first quarter, but sales of its top-selling drugs were well up.
Roche said in a first quarter statement that without the falls in Rivotril/Klonopin and Toradol, global sales for the pharmaceuticals division would have exceeded six percent in local currencies.
However, "the growth trend for the division's major established products and new entries remained unchanged," Roche said.

Roche's sales from its pharma division rose 19 percent in Swiss franc terms to 2.89 billion Swiss francs in the first quarter from the same 1996 period, but in local currencies sales rose three percent.
Worldwide sales of Roche's top-selling drugs were well up in the first quarter with Rocephin, Neupogen, Ticlid posting double-digit gains in local currencies.
In the Over-The-Counter (OTC) segment of the market, sales were also up by two digit figures in local currencies.
Sales of Invirase rose far ahead of the high growth that had been forecast and CellCept sales more than doubled in local currencies.
Sales of Rivotril/Klonopin fell due to competition from several generic drugs since October 1996 while sales of Toradol fell to a lesser extent after the launch of a generic competitor was announced.
"Without these drops in sales, which were sharper than expected, global sales growth for the divison would have exceeded six percent in local currencies," Roche said.
First quarter sales were well ahead of average growth in important European markets, such as Germany, Italy and Spain as well as Canada and Brazil.
In France sales were steady in local currency terms, despite government action to curb market growth.
Sales declined slightly in Japan as the market slowed in anticipation of the government-mandated price cut that came into effect on April 1, Roche said.
